runs.runA: Under Florida Statute 692.203, foreign principals from countries of concern are prohibited from purchasing real property within 20 miles of military installations. A natural person with a valid visa may purchase one residential property of up to 5 acres if it is at least 10 miles from a military installation. Owners must register with the Department of State, and late registration carries a $500 daily fine. Violations are a first-degree misdemeanor.

runs.runA: Florida Statute 692.203 bars foreign principals from owning real property near sensitive facilities. The exclusion zone is 10 miles around military bases and 25 miles around critical infrastructure. Individuals with non-tourist visas may buy a single home on up to 1 acre outside a 5-mile radius of any base. Registration with the Department of Commerce was required by June 30, 2024, with $1,000 daily fines for late filing. Violations can lead to forfeiture and third-degree felony charges.

From the source text:

1. The prohibition covers real property on or within 10 miles of any military installation or critical infrastructure facility (subsection 1).

2. A natural person may purchase one residential property up to 2 acres in size, provided the parcel is not on or within 5 miles of any military installation and the buyer holds a current verified non-tourist visa or asylum documentation (subsection 4).

3. Property owned before July 1, 2023 may be retained but no additional property may be acquired (subsection 2). The registration deadline for pre-existing interests was December 31, 2023, considered late after January 31, 2024 (subsection 3(b)).

4. Violations by buyer or seller are second-degree misdemeanors (subsections 8 and 9).
